examples.en: It's year-end, so I push myself hard with overtime every day.
After pushing myself all week, I came down with body aches.

examples.ko: 여행 첫날부터 강행군하지 말고 쉬엄쉬엄 다녀요.
examples.en: Don't push too hard from the first day of the trip; take it easy.

examples.ko: 시험 기간에는 밤늦게까지 강행군하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: During exams, many students push themselves until late at night.

examples.ko: 이번 출장은 다섯 도시를 돌며 강행군해야 해요.
examples.en: On this business trip, I have to keep up a punishing pace visiting five cities.

examples.ko: 촬영팀이 새벽부터 밤까지 강행군해서 모두 지쳤어요.
examples.en: The filming crew worked flat out from dawn to night, so everyone is exhausted.

explain: 일정이 빡빡해서 쉬지 못하고 무리하게 계속 움직이거나 일할 때 써요. '강행군을 하다', '강행군이다'로도 자주 말해요. 반대로 여유 있게 다니는 건 '쉬엄쉬엄'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes keeping on moving or working at a tight, exhausting pace without rest. People also say '강행군을 하다' or '강행군이다'. A relaxed pace is described with '쉬엄쉬엄'.

examples.en: My grandfather is very learned, so he knows everything.
Thanks to our learned teacher, the class is fun.
That writer is famous for being widely learned.
My friend called me widely learned, and I felt shy.
He may look learned, but there are many fields he doesn't know.
I think being widely learned is not the same as being wise.

explain: 학문이 넓고 아는 것이 많다는 사자성어예요. 보통 '박학다식하다', '박학다식한'처럼 형용사처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '아는 게 많다'나 '척척박사'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom means being broadly learned and knowing a lot. It is usually used like an adjective, as in '박학다식하다' and '박학다식한'. In daily talk people also say '아는 게 많다' or '척척박사'.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 업무 분업화가 잘 되어 있어요.
examples.en: Our company has a well-organized division of labor.
Thanks to the division of labor, the work got much faster.
Division of labor is very important in a factory.

examples.ko: 지나친 분업화는 오히려 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Too much specialization can actually become a problem.

examples.ko: 요즘은 작업의 분업화를 줄이는 팀도 있어요.
examples.en: These days some teams are reducing the division of tasks.
The higher the level of specialization, the simpler each job becomes.

explain: '분업'이 일을 나눠서 하는 것 자체라면, '분업화'는 그렇게 나뉘어 가는 과정이나 정도를 말할 때 많이 써요. 회사, 공장, 산업 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 반대로 합치는 쪽은 '통합'이라고 해요.
explain_en: If '분업' is the act of splitting up work, '분업화' is used more for the process or degree of that splitting. It often comes up when talking about companies, factories and industries. The opposite direction is '통합' (integration).

examples.en: The team members divided up the work and finished quickly.
If you divide up the work, mistakes decrease.
This shop splits ordering and packing between different people.
Dividing up the tasks is harder than I thought.
How about we divide up the cleaning too?
After we divided up the work, efficiency went up.

explain: 일상에서는 '일을 나눠서 하다'라고 더 자주 말하고, '분업화하다'는 회사나 공장 같은 조직 이야기에서 써요. '일을 분업화하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. 반대로 합치는 쪽은 '통합하다'예요.
explain_en: In daily talk people more often say '일을 나눠서 하다', while '분업화하다' fits talk about organizations such as companies and factories. It takes an object, as in '일을 분업화하다'. The opposite direction is '통합하다' (to integrate).

examples.en: They link schools and companies to run practical training.
The hospital works in connection with the local welfare center.
If you link the shopping app to your card, you get a discount.
It is an activity that ties the lesson to daily life.

examples.ko: 다른 팀과 연계하려면 먼저 연락해야 해요.
examples.en: To coordinate with another team, you need to contact them first.

examples.ko: 두 서비스를 연계하는 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We're looking for a way to link the two services.

explain: 'A를 B와 연계하다'로 써요. 사람이나 기관이 일부러 이어 붙인다는 느낌이에요. 저절로 이어지면 '연계되다'예요. '연결하다'가 선·길·전화처럼 실제로 잇는 말이라면, '연계하다'는 제도·서비스·수업 같은 추상적인 것에 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used as 'A를 B와 연계하다', and the subject is a person or organization that links things on purpose. When the link happens by itself, use 연계되다. 연결하다 is for physically joining things like lines, roads or phone calls, while 연계하다 suits abstract things such as systems, services and classes.

examples.en: My father does the work of welding steel plates.
I welded the two pipes together into one.

examples.ko: 처음 용접할 때는 손이 많이 떨렸어요.
examples.en: My hands shook a lot the first time I welded.

examples.ko: 이 부분은 꼭 전문가가 용접해야 해요.
examples.en: This part must be welded by a professional.
After I welded the iron gate, it became much sturdier.

examples.ko: 용접하기 전에 표면을 깨끗이 닦아 주세요.
examples.en: Please clean the surface well before welding.

explain: '철판을 용접하다'처럼 금속을 목적어로 써요. 금속을 열로 녹여 붙이는 것이라서 접착제나 테이프로 붙일 때는 '붙이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It takes metal as its object, as in '철판을 용접하다'. Since it means fusing metal with heat, you say '붙이다' when sticking things with glue or tape.

examples.en: Fatigue builds up in the body.
When long experience accumulates, your skill grows.
Knowledge does not accumulate overnight.
The more data accumulates, the more accurate the results get.
Heat has built up in the room, so it is hot.

examples.ko: 이 기술은 수십 년 동안 축적된 노력의 결과예요.
examples.en: This technology is the result of effort accumulated over decades.

explain: '쌓이다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 경험·지식·자료·피로처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 먼지나 눈처럼 눈에 보이는 것은 '쌓이다'가 더 자연스러워요. 사람이 모으는 쪽은 '축적하다'예요.
explain_en: A stiffer word than '쌓이다', often used for invisible things like experience, knowledge, data and fatigue. For visible things like dust or snow, '쌓이다' sounds more natural. The person-does-it form is '축적하다'.
